column1: # finding-classes.tsv (t-70f2) — the one table of finding classes: slug, meaning, the reviewer concern it falls under. Tab-separated; a slug is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

# A gate ends each finding with `class: <slug>` from here; `canon-go finding-classes` counts them across tickets. skills/sprint/reference/review.md lists the same slugs and tests/doc-mirror-parity.sh fails when the two differ. Add a slug in both places.

column2: more code, files or abstraction than the change needs
a path, id, limit or value written in code that a table, argument or the environment owns
a changed file the plan did not name
the same fact or logic in a second place instead of one owner
a doc, comment or mirror that no longer matches the code
a test or check that passes whatever the code does
a failure turned into a normal-looking result
input the code does not control is trusted, executed or printed
a path, shell, platform or tool difference that breaks on another machine
a real finding that fits no class above
